item.title: Space station experiment to probe plant disease risks for future moon and Mars missions
item.description: As NASA and its partners prepare for longer human missions beyond Earth, University of Florida researchers are investigating a challenge that could affect astronauts' ability to grow fresh food in space: plant disease.

item.title: NASA's new UV space telescope will launch in 2031
item.description: Most of us could spend our entire lives looking at the night sky and see very few changes. The moon becomes more or less illuminated, the planets drift placidly through the sky, satellites and the ISS intrude for a few moments at a time, and the bright, momentary streak of a meteor punctuates the occasional evening of stargazing.

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 conserves power, resolves brief communications pause
item.description: NASA's Voyager team is celebrating two recent developments with the Voyager 1 spacecraft: In September, they successfully completed a months-long effort to stretch the spacecraft's diminishing power supply. Then, on Oct. 20, an unexpected loss of communication with the spacecraft resolved itself after 48 hours, before the team sent commands to the spacecraft to troubleshoot the issue.

item.title: Rusty crust made Mars warm and wet
item.description: It's unclear how and why Mars once became warm enough to allow water to flow on its surface, but a new idea suggests it comes down to rust below the surface

item.title: Built to take the blast: Students test prototype landing pad to make moon landings safer
item.description: As NASA works toward a sustained human presence on the moon, researchers at The University of Alabama in Huntsville (UAH), a part of The University of Alabama System, are helping solve one of the most pressing challenges facing future lunar missions: how to land spacecraft safely without damaging the landing vehicle or nearby infrastructure.

item.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
item.description: The Martian Moons eXploration ( MMX ) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. item.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
item.description: Scientists using the European Space Agency's Mars Express , in combination with a state-of-the-art meteorological model of the Red Planet, have found that there may be some very exotic physics behind Mars’s most curious cloud.

item.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.

item.description: Acting as cooperative optical beacons, the satellites could provide GPS-like navigation and communications support for spacecraft operating across cislunar space.

item.title: Study: Rocks from Mars’ Jezero Crater, which likely predate life on Earth, contain signs of water
item.description: The presence of organic matter is inconclusive, but the rocks could be scientists’ best chance at finding remnants of ancient Martian life.

item.title: Study determines the original orientations of rocks drilled on Mars
item.description: The “oriented” samples, the first of their kind from any planet, could shed light on Mars’ ancient magnetic field.

item.title: Fly around Schiaparelli Crater with Mars Express
item.description: Video: 00:04:10 ESA’s Mars Express takes us on another mesmerising flight, this time around one of the biggest craters on Mars. Despite measuring a huge 460 km across, Schiaparelli Crater seems to be relatively shallow. Perhaps it has been filled in over the last few billion years by sediment blown by the wind or deposited by water, by lava – or by a combination of all three. item.description: PhD candidate Lanie McKinney is building technology to convert the Red Planet’s atmosphere into propellant for bringing astronauts home.

item.title: Lincoln Laboratory laser communications terminal launches on historic Artemis II moon mission
item.description: High-definition video and data sent from the lunar vicinity to Earth will demonstrate the first use of laser communications on a crewed mission.

item.description: The barely-there lunar atmosphere is likely the product of meteorite impacts over billions of years, a new study finds.
